
shadshiny's look is entirely token-driven. Every colour, radius, and surface is
a CSS custom property, so theming means overriding properties — never editing
component CSS or hard-coding hex values.

## The token system

Colours are OKLCH `--shad-*` custom properties defined on the page root, for
example `--shad-background`, `--shad-foreground`, `--shad-primary`,
`--shad-muted`, `--shad-border`, `--shad-ring`. Components reference these
tokens exclusively. To restyle, set the token — not the element.

```css
/* your own CSS, included via page_shad(..., tags$head(...)) or a www/ file */
:root {
  --shad-primary: oklch(0.55 0.22 265);
  --shad-radius: 0.75rem;
}
```

Because everything keys off the same variables, one override cascades through
every component consistently in both light and dark mode.

## The seven presets

shadshiny ships seven palettes: **slate, stone, blue, green, rose, violet,
orange**. Choose one at the page level:

```{r}
library(shadshiny)
page_shad(theme_preset = "green")
```

Presets are applied through a `data-shad-theme` attribute on the page root, so
they compose with — rather than replace — your custom token overrides.

Scope a preset to one subtree when the rest of the page should keep its current
palette:

```{r}
shad_theme_preset(
  "green",
  shad_card(shad_card_content("Only this card uses the green preset."))
)
```

## Dark mode

Dark mode keys off `.dark` **and** `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` on an ancestor.
That second signal is exactly what `bslib::input_dark_mode()` toggles, so a
bslib dark-mode switch drives shadshiny components with zero extra wiring:

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(shadshiny)

page_shad(
  input_dark_mode(),          # toggles [data-bs-theme]; shadshiny follows
  shad_card(shad_card_content(shad_p("I recolour automatically.")))
)
```

You can also force a mode at page level:

```{r}
page_shad(dark = TRUE, ...)   # start in dark mode
```

## Directionality

`page_shad()` accepts ordinary HTML attributes through `...`, so an RTL page
does not add a new R API argument:

```{r}
page_shad(dir = "rtl", lang = "ar", shad_p("واجهة عربية"))
```

The runtime keeps floating panels and other body portals synchronized with the
nearest `dir` and `lang` owner, including direction changes made after the
page loads. Layout spacing, borders, and alignment use CSS logical properties;
physical coordinates remain explicit where a component's named side is a
geometry contract. For user content that can mix scripts, opt into browser
script detection with `dir = "auto"` on the content wrapper, message content,
or data-table root (for example, `shad_data_table("tbl", data, dir = "auto")`).

## Changing theme at runtime

`update_shad_theme()` swaps the preset and/or dark state live from the server —
ideal for a settings toolbar built from a `shad_select()` and a `shad_switch()`:

```{r}
ui <- page_shad(
  shad_select("preset", label = "Theme",
              choices = c("slate", "stone", "blue", "green",
                          "rose", "violet", "orange"),
              selected = "slate"),
  shad_switch("dark", label = "Dark mode")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe({
    update_shad_theme(preset = input$preset, dark = input$dark)
  })
}
```

## Custom themes

The seven presets are a starting point, not a ceiling. `shad_theme()` builds a
palette in R: name the tokens you care about, leave the rest to the base.

```{r}
brand <- shad_theme(
  primary            = "#7c3aed",
  primary_foreground = "#ffffff",
  radius             = "0.75rem",
  font_sans          = "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif",
  chart              = c("#7c3aed", "#06b6d4", "#f59e0b", "#ef4444"),
  dark = list(primary = "#a78bfa", background = "oklch(0.16 0.02 285)")
)

ui <- page_shad(theme = brand, ...)
```

Colours may be hex (`"#7c3aed"`), `rgb()`, a named CSS colour, or OKLCH
(`"oklch(0.55 0.24 285)"`) — everything is normalised on the way in. `dark =`
takes a list of the same token names, applied only under `.dark`; tokens you
don't name there inherit the light value, which is almost never what you want
for `background` and `foreground`.

The named arguments cover the common tokens (`primary`, `background`,
`foreground`, `card`, `muted`, `accent`, `destructive`, `border`, `input`,
`ring`, `radius`, `font_sans`, `font_mono`, and their `*_foreground` pairs).
Anything else — including the `--shad-sidebar-*` family — goes through `...`
with the `--shad-` prefix dropped:

```{r}
shad_theme(primary = "#7c3aed", `sidebar-background` = "oklch(0.98 0.01 285)")
```

### Scoping a theme

`theme =` on `page_shad()` themes the whole page. To theme one region instead,
wrap it:

```{r}
shad_theme_scope(
  brand,
  shad_card(shad_card_content("Only this subtree uses `brand`."))
)
```

`shad_theme_scope()` mints a private class and emits the CSS for it, so nested
scopes compose and nothing leaks out.

### Importing from the shadcn registry

The [shadcn theme registry](https://ui.shadcn.com/themes) publishes themes as
JSON. `shad_theme_from_registry()` maps their token names onto shadshiny's and
hands you back a `shad_theme()`. The import is experimental: the registry
schema belongs to upstream and may move.

```{r}
tw <- shad_theme_from_registry("https://tweakcn.com/r/themes/some-theme.json")
ui <- page_shad(theme = tw, ...)
```

It takes a URL or a local path. Unmapped tokens are dropped rather than
guessed, so a registry theme built for a much newer shadcn will land, minus
whatever shadshiny has no slot for.

### Switching a custom theme at runtime

`update_shad_theme(theme = )` takes a `shad_theme()` just like `preset =` takes
a preset name, and `theme = NA` clears back to the page's own:

```{r}
observeEvent(input$brand_on,  update_shad_theme(theme = brand))
observeEvent(input$brand_off, update_shad_theme(theme = NA))
```

### Reading the tokens back

`shad_tokens(preset, dark)` returns the resolved token set, and
`shad_chart_colors(n, preset, dark)` the chart ramp as hex — both useful when
you need to hand a colour to something that isn't CSS, like a plot. See
`vignette("charts")`.

## Hand-written CSS

You never have to use `shad_theme()`. The tokens are ordinary custom
properties, so plain CSS works. The sidebar family has its own `--shad-sidebar-*` tokens
(`--shad-sidebar-background`, `--shad-sidebar-foreground`,
`--shad-sidebar-border`, …) so you can give navigation a distinct surface:

```css
:root {
  --shad-sidebar-background: oklch(0.98 0.01 265);
}
.dark {
  --shad-sidebar-background: oklch(0.20 0.02 265);
}
```

Override under both the light selector and `.dark` to keep the two modes in
step.
